## Field snapshot (as of the cutoff)
Three to five years ago, prompt-injection work consisted of demonstrations and hand-written attack catalogues (Greshake et al. 2023). In 2024, fixed-data training defenses (StruQ, instruction-hierarchy training, SecAlign) and the AgentDojo benchmark made agent-level evaluation standard. In 2025, system-level defenses (CaMeL, MELON, Task Shield, RTBAS, DRIFT) reported near-zero ASR with small utility losses on closed models, while adaptive-attack work showed that many defenses break under tailored attacks; automated red-teaming with RL (diverse-attack RL, self-play safety) matured for chat models. Open problems stated by recent work: robustness against adaptive attackers, utility preservation, and transfer across agent frameworks. What counts as significant now: a defense that stays effective under adaptive, independently generated attacks on a standard benchmark such as AgentDojo, or a learned-attacker method that beats fixed-data fine-tuning at equal budget; a 1-point ASR change on a benchmark with a 1–6% base rate is not significant.
